prompt: Put the three blocks of an executive summary in order.
Why does the lesson say to write the page as if it were the only trace of the work?

choices.text: Because it is forwarded, filed and found again later
choices.why: Often it is the only thing that survives.

choices.text: The deck will be deleted
choices.why: Nothing says so.

choices.text: Pages are cheaper to store
choices.why: Not the argument.

choices.text: Analysts cannot present to the board
choices.why: No such rule.

prompt: What goes in the header of the page? Choose all that apply.
hint: What a busy reader scans first.

choices.text: Who it is for
choices.why: The reader sees it is theirs.

choices.text: Who it is from
choices.why: So the reader knows who to ask.

choices.text: The date a decision is needed by
choices.why: It turns information into a request with a deadline.

choices.text: The method of the analysis
choices.why: Method belongs to the full analysis.

prompt: Why one page rather than two?

choices.text: Printers cost money
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: Each sentence has to displace another, and one page gets read
choices.why: Two pages invite skimming.

choices.text: It is a legal limit
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Executives do not read the second page of anything they are sent by an analyst
choices.why: An overstatement the lesson does not make.

prompt: Which clause in Faro's finding answers an objection before it is raised?
hint: Lesson 10 deals with it at length.

choices.text: One new subscriber in six
choices.why: That gives the size a picture.

choices.text: Against 17.4% for everybody else
choices.why: That is the comparison, not an answered objection.

choices.text: In the first half of 2025, counted from the first box of each new subscription
choices.why: That is the period and the definition.

choices.text: The gap holds in both regions
choices.why: It closes the question whether region explains it.

prompt: What separates a caveat from a hedge, by the lesson?

choices.text: A caveat is shorter
choices.why: Length is not the difference.

choices.text: It names a limit and its weight
choices.why: A hedge weakens every sentence without saying why.

choices.text: Hedges go in the appendix, caveats in the text
choices.why: They go nowhere.

choices.text: A caveat uses numbers
choices.why: It might, and that is not the distinction.

prompt: Why does the page write 17.3% rather than 17.30% or "about 20%"?

choices.text: Because 17.30% is the exact figure
choices.why: It claims a precision the data does not support.

choices.text: Round numbers are banned
choices.why: No such ban.

choices.text: Honest precision that matches the slide
choices.why: "About 20%" would make the page disagree with the deck.

choices.text: The template only allows one decimal place in every number it displays
choices.why: Not the reason.

prompt: The calculation gives R$ 792,611.40. Why does the page say "about R$ 790 thousand"?

choices.text: Its inputs are estimates, so eight figures overclaim
choices.why: Count precisely, estimate roughly.

choices.text: To make it sound bigger
choices.why: It is rounded down, and size is not the point.

choices.text: Finance prefers round numbers
choices.why: Not the reason given.

choices.text: Centavos cannot go on a slide
choices.why: They can; they should not here.

prompt: How many extra early cancellations a year does the impact block cite?
Why should an impact block say what happens if nothing is done?

choices.text: It is required by finance policy
choices.why: No.

choices.text: Because doing nothing is the default
choices.why: It turns "interesting" into "worth deciding this week".

choices.text: To scare the reader
choices.why: It states a cost, calmly.

choices.text: So the reader can compare it with last year's figures for the same period
choices.why: Not the purpose.

prompt: Where should the arithmetic behind the R$ 790 thousand live?
hint: Renata will want to check it.

choices.text: On the page, under the impact
choices.why: It would push out something the decision needs.

choices.text: Nowhere: the result is enough
choices.why: A finance director who wants to check must be able to.

choices.text: In the full analysis
choices.why: The page shows the results; the analysis shows the arithmetic.

choices.text: In an email to finance only, sent separately after the decision has been taken
choices.why: After the decision is too late to check it.

prompt: What verb opens Faro's next step?

choices.text: Approve
choices.why: A decision the reader performs.

choices.text: Consider
choices.why: Asks for thought, not a decision.

choices.text: Note
choices.why: Asks for nothing.

choices.text: It is recommended
choices.why: No subject, asks nobody.

prompt: Why is the test of success written before the pilot starts?

choices.text: Because the board requires a target
choices.why: Not the reason.

choices.text: To make the pilot look ambitious
choices.why: It is about fairness, not ambition.

choices.text: Because the data team needs it to set up the dashboard tiles before the start
choices.why: Useful, and not the reason given.

choices.text: Else the loudest opinion wins
choices.why: A test decided afterwards is decided by whoever argues hardest.

prompt: Faro's next step names a risk as its cost. Why?

choices.text: Because there is no money cost to report
choices.why: True, and naming the risk is about trust, not filling a field.

choices.text: Naming it first makes the page trustworthy
choices.why: Mis-delivered boxes are the honest cost of removing the check.

choices.text: To lower expectations
choices.why: It states a fact; expectations are set by the test.

choices.text: Legal reasons
choices.why: None given.

prompt: The checklist: a reader could reply with one word, ___.
Which part of the page does Sandra read first, by the lesson?

choices.text: The header
choices.why: That is Paulo's way in.

choices.text: The finding
choices.why: Not her first stop.

choices.text: The last sentence of the impact
choices.why: It names the cause in her warehouse; then she reads the next step, which gives her team the fix.

choices.text: The pointer to the full analysis
choices.why: That is Renata's route.

prompt: What test of a summary does the section draw from four readers reading in four orders?
hint: Will it get a reading order?

choices.text: It must not assume a reading order
choices.why: Each block has to stand on its own.

choices.text: It must be read top to bottom
choices.why: The section shows that it is not.

choices.text: It must have four sections
choices.why: It has three blocks.

choices.text: It must be signed by every reader
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson.

prompt: On what day of October 2025 is the pilot reviewed?
Match each reader to the block they go to first.

pairs.right: The cause, at the end of the impact

prompt: This page has no words. Put each label on the part of an executive summary it names.
hint: Three blocks, in their usual order, between a header and a footer.
